Sample Name: General Medicine Followup - Diabetes and Knee Pain
Description: Follow-up for diabetes, hypertension, and recurrent knee pain with discussion of weight management.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient returns for review of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes. A higher dose of metformin was introduced recently, and adherence to diabetes and antihypertensive medications was reviewed. He missed lisinopril this morning and has elevated office blood pressure. Prior urine testing showed marked glycosuria. Insulin was discussed as a future option if oral agents become inadequate, not as treatment initiated today. He is interested in exercise and reducing weight but reports practical constraints related to work and neighborhood safety. Right knee pain has returned despite icing and ibuprofen. He previously underwent surgery for a cartilage injury. He also requests medication for erectile dysfunction.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Diabetes, hypertension, obesity, recurrent right knee pain following prior surgery, and erectile dysfunction.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Weight approximately 252-253 lb by the patient's report. Right knee without substantial visible swelling; some clinical crepitus and discomfort are noted.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Diabetes: Continue recently adjusted oral regimen and emphasize daily adherence. Repeat hemoglobin A1c after an appropriate interval. Discussed diet, exercise, and eventual insulin only if oral treatment fails.
2. Hypertension: Elevated after missed lisinopril dose; resume consistent therapy and reassess.
3. Recurrent knee pain: Obtain imaging and arrange Orthopedics assessment to determine whether further studies or intervention are indicated.
4. Obesity: Reviewed MOVE lifestyle program and accessible exercise.
5. Erectile dysfunction: Initiate lower-dose vardenafil and review response and side effects at follow-up.
6. Immunization: Tdap booster arranged; influenza vaccination previously received. Colonoscopy appointment reviewed.
